entries.summary: JEP 401 (Value Objects) arrives in OpenJDK as a preview feature, enabling a new Java type model with minimal code changes.
entries.text: JEP 401 (Value Objects) arrives in OpenJDK as a preview feature, enabling a new Java type model with minimal code changes. The talk explains what value objects are, JVM benefits, Valhalla history, implementation details, and the path toward bridging objects and primitives, including future support like List<int>.
entries.title: Why It Takes 3000 Commits to Bring Valhalla’s Value Objects to the JDK

entries.summary: Modern software increasingly interacts with AI models, query languages, and other specialized programming models, forcing you to switch contexts, embed foreign code, or write verbose wrappers to bridge the gap.
entries.text: Modern software increasingly interacts with AI models, query languages, and other specialized programming models, forcing you to switch contexts, embed foreign code, or write verbose wrappers to bridge the gap. What if you could express logic from outside the JVM directly in Java? In this session, we start by looking at how Java enables you to safely interact with runtimes outside of the JVM using the Foreign Function and Memory API and tools like jextract. Then will push further with Project Babylon’s code reflection: express AI models as Java programs that Babylon can analyze, transform and lower to inference engines, thus leveraging hardware accelerator backends while skipping external model files or the need to glue code.
entries.title: Java and the Next Generation of Programming Models

entries.summary: Interacting with foreign libraries from Java has never been easier, thanks to the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API. But interacting with entire foreign language runtimes, like JavaScript or Python, remains hard.
entries.text: Interacting with foreign libraries from Java has never been easier, thanks to the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API. But interacting with entire foreign language runtimes, like JavaScript or Python, remains hard. Project Detroit paves a new way forward: instead of implementing bespoke language runtimes from scratch, it leverages FFM to embed industry-standard native runtimes like V8 and CPython in the safety and comfort of your Java application.
entries.title: Project Detroit: From Foreign Libraries to Foreign Language Runtimes
